back: Ground distance (km) = map distance (cm) × scale denominator ÷ 100 000.
Vertical interval ÷ horizontal distance (same unit). Written 1 in n, where n = horizontal ÷ vertical, or as a percentage.
Eastings first, then northings ('along the corridor, up the stairs'). Six figures include tenths of a square.

front: What do close and wide contours show?
back: Close together: steep slope. Wide apart: gentle slope.

front: Contour patterns for valleys and spurs?
back: Valley: V-shapes pointing uphill. Spur or ridge: V-shapes pointing downhill.
The bearing in the reverse direction: the bearing ± 180°.
Dendritic (uniform rock), radial (from a hill), trellis (alternating hard and soft rocks), parallel (uniform slope), centripetal (into a basin).
Channel length ÷ straight-line length; above about 1.5 is meandering.
Compare the height of any ridge between the two points with the straight line of sight between them.

front: How to measure a curved route on a map?
back: Lay thread or a paper strip along the route, straighten it and measure it against the scale bar.
